 H_r(S)=J_r(T_r S)/(kappa sigma^2),
 c_r=1/[201326592(1+r^4)].

The previously received N901 theorem proves the strong ACTUAL Hessian
inequality for H_r, at every symmetric mean, with coefficient c_r.

Theorem A. There are explicit finite positive coefficients K2(r),K4(r)
such that the HOMOGENEOUS QUARTIC

 Jhat_r(A)=J_r(A)+K2 U(A)^2 |S(A)|^2+K4 U(A)^4             (1)

is globally quasiconvex and rank-one convex on ALL real 2 by 2 matrices,
at ALL affine means and for ALL actual W^(1,4) gradient perturbations.
It agrees exactly with J_r on U=0, and its first derivative normal to
that plane agrees there as well. The original mixed coupling is retained.

This is a theorem about the explicitly corrected quartic (1). It does
not prove general-U quasiconvexity of uncorrected J_r. It provides a
finite degree-four completion and a full variational estimate on general
compatible fields; it does not identify an outer bound with attainable
capacity.
